artworks.title: The Return of Idomeneus
artworks.description: Jacques Gamelin's painting of the Cretan king's nostos, now in the Musée des Augustins (Palais Niel), Toulouse, stages the storm-tossed return that will force Idomeneus into his fatal vow to Neptune. The canvas belongs to the French academic tradition that treated Homeric homecomings as moral dramas of oath, sacrifice, and exile.

artworks.title: Megarian bowl with Idomeneus (fragmentary)
artworks.description: A fragmentary Megarian relief bowl in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (1980.11.2a–c) names the Cretan king in clay: from left to right, inscribed Idomeneus attacks Phaistos as he steps into his chariot, while Athena and Ares watch Homeric duels from the banks of the Skamandros. The bowl closely follows Iliad 5 — one of the rare ancient vessels to label Idomeneus by name.

artworks.title: Hegesippus Summons Philocles at Idomeneus' Request
artworks.description: An etching from the 1785 Didot edition of Fénelon's Les Aventures de Télémaque shows Idomeneus seated beneath a tree reading a letter while Hegesippus stands beside him. In Fénelon's political romance the Homeric Cretan king becomes a ruler whose court Telemachus must navigate — the mythological Idomeneus translated into Enlightenment didactic fiction.

music.title: Idomeneo
music.description: Mozart's opera seria of the Cretan king's vow to Neptune — Idamante, Ilia, and a storm-born sacrifice rewrite the nostos.

popCulture.title: Idomeneus
popCulture.description: King of Crete's hundred cities — Homeric champion whose return ends in usurpation and exile in the later catalogues.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.description: Homer's Cretan captain — Poseidon walks the field in his likeness at Troy before the nostos that will undo him.
